purpose: Buffer vessel working volume and impeller submergence
notes: Monitoring only: no control row references it. The minimum working volume that makes this reading meaningful is itself unknown (Q-049), which is why U00-BUF carries a turndown basis rather than a turndown ratio.

purpose: Buffer hold temperature
notes: Monitoring only. The ligation buffer is growth-promoting and the whole train is aqueous, so hold temperature and hold time together drive the contamination-control strategy (R-009, Q-043).

purpose: Prepared-buffer strength and identity check before release to the reactor
notes: Monitoring only. A conductivity check catches a mis-charged buffer; it does not establish composition, which is in buffers.csv (BUF-LIG).

purpose: Prepared-buffer pH before release to the reactor
notes: Monitoring only.

purpose: Bioburden sample point on the buffer hold
notes: Monitoring only. Non-sterile microbiological quality is a compendial expectation (SRC-PHEUR-5-1-4); the hold-time limits that would set the sampling frequency do not exist for this train (Q-043, R-009).

purpose: Endotoxin sample point on the water and buffer entering the train
notes: Monitoring only. Water for injections is controlled for bacterial endotoxins by its monograph (SRC-PHEUR-0169); this is the entry point for the endotoxin load that R-017 says a cell-free extract route would add to downstream of it.

purpose: Ligation reaction temperature control
notes: Enforces P-LIG-T. The setpoint is a placeholder: 25 C is what both cited ligation examples ran at, but the optimum moves with the enzyme and its form, which is undecided (Q-050).

purpose: Reactor working volume and low-shear mixing at low fill
notes: Monitoring only.

purpose: ATP concentration in the charged ligation buffer, by HPLC
notes: Enforces P-LIG-ATP, and it is OFF-line by nature: ATP is fixed by what is weighed into the buffer, not trimmed during the reaction. The setpoint itself is contested - four ligations want at least 4 mM while suppressing the adenylylated dead end wants under 100 uM, and no source resolves it (Q-040, R-010).

purpose: Ligation conversion, in-process control
notes: Enforces P-LIG-CONV (EQ-LIG). At-line rather than in-line: conversion is a chromatographic measurement on a withdrawn sample. Note that the strongest engineered-ligase source reports RELATIVE PEAK AREA only and so does not itself set an acceptance value (SRC-USPTO-10640812, Q-010, Q-050).

purpose: Adenylylated dead-end (AppN) species by LC-MS
notes: Monitoring only, because no control is defined: the AppN dead end was observed in exactly this chemistry (SRC-ALMAC-2023) and it is ~329 Da from the product, so filtration cannot remove it (R-010). This instrument can see the defect; nothing in the register yet prevents it (Q-040).

purpose: Bioburden sample point on the ligation pool
notes: Monitoring only.

purpose: Differential pressure across the depth filter; capacity endpoint
notes: Monitoring only. The throughput (L/m2) that would turn this into a sized endpoint is a gap (Q-036).

purpose: Differential pressure across the 0.2 um filter
notes: Monitoring only.

purpose: Filtrate flow through the clarification train
notes: Monitoring only.

purpose: Residual ligase / total protein in the clarified pool
notes: The single instrument the chromatography-free thesis rests on, and it enforces BOTH branches of Q-050 - a soluble enzyme denatured and filtered, or one retained on a carrier - because either way what must be demonstrated is protein absence in this pool. Its acceptance value (P-ENZ-CLEARANCE-LRV) is BLANK: no ppm, log-reduction or immunoassay figure for ligase clearance exists in the public record (Q-032, R-002).

purpose: Endotoxin in the clarified pool
notes: Monitoring only. A cell-free-extract route puts a whole proteome plus endotoxin through this point rather than one enzyme (R-017), so the load this instrument sees depends on Q-050.

purpose: Clarified-pool temperature
notes: Monitoring only, and NOT the denature hold. The soluble branch of Q-050 needs an 85 C/15 min hold, which needs a heated vessel or exchanger; U02-CF is single-use depth media and cannot denature anything. That unit does not exist in the equipment register and its absence is registered against Q-050 (R-021).

purpose: Feed pressure control on the TFF skid
Transmembrane pressure (TMP)
notes: The operating handle for flux (EQ-FLUX). Which mechanism actually sets the ceiling - osmotic pressure or fouling - is open (Q-041), so TMP is instrumented but its limit is not set.

purpose: Permeate flow, i.e. flux
notes: Enforces the flux the membrane area is sized from (EQ-FLUX). The flux value itself is carried on surrogates and is a gap for an oligonucleotide stream (Q-036).

purpose: Retentate recirculation flow; minimum channel crossflow velocity
notes: Monitoring only. Crossflow velocity is what sets the skid's turndown (Q-049).

purpose: Diafiltration endpoint by permeate conductivity
notes: Enforces P-DF-DIAVOL (EQ-DIAF). IN-LINE conductivity is not in question and is instrumented as such; what cannot be read in line is UV, and only at the concentrations this stream reaches - at P-CONC-UF the required path length falls below P-VPE-PATHLENGTH-MIN (Q-042). The two were advertised together as 'in-line UV/conductivity' before this register separated them.

purpose: Retentate concentration, at-line by variable-pathlength slope spectroscopy
notes: AT-LINE ON THIS STREAM, and that is a geometric constraint rather than a property of the instrument class. Fixed-pathlength in-line UV saturates on a 21-mer at process concentration, and at P-CONC-UF the pathlength an A260 = 1 reading needs falls below the published in-line floor P-VPE-PATHLENGTH-MIN, so the reading is taken on a withdrawn sample. An earlier version of this row said variable-pathlength slope spectroscopy is inherently at-line; that was WRONG - FlowVPE publishes 5 um to 8 mm and is used in-line on UF/DF (SRC-ROLINGER-2023, SRC-BHANGALE-2022). It serves control C-013, whose loop is therefore open. See Q-051 for what would have to close first.

purpose: Product loss to permeate
notes: Monitoring only. Off-line on a grab sample; sieving and the resulting yield term are open (EQ-SIEVE, EQ-UFYIELD, Q-036, Q-048).

purpose: Retentate vessel level and system hold-up
notes: Monitoring only. Hold-up volume is part of both the turndown basis (Q-049) and the yield loss term (P-UFDF-HOLDUP-LOSS).

purpose: Bioburden sample point on the retentate
notes: Monitoring only.

purpose: Vacuum boiling temperature
notes: Enforces P-EVAP-T-BOIL, the thermal operating point the sensible-heat duty is computed from (EQ-ENERGY, EQ-BPE). The value is an assumption (Q-045).

purpose: Evaporator absolute pressure (vacuum)
notes: The handle that sets the boiling temperature above (EQ-BPE). Monitoring and control of the operating point, not of a quality attribute.

purpose: Feed temperature to the evaporator
notes: Monitoring only. P-EVAP-T-FEED sets how much sensible heat is needed before anything evaporates (EQ-ENERGY).

purpose: Feed flow, against the minimum wetting rate per unit tube perimeter
notes: Monitoring only, but it is the reading that shows whether the evaporator can run at all at a small batch size: below the minimum wetting rate the film breaks into rivulets, so a small batch must recirculate rather than run single-pass (P-EVAP-MIN-WETRATE, R-013, R-004).

purpose: Condensate flow, i.e. water actually removed
notes: Monitoring only; closes the evaporator water balance against the computed figure.

purpose: Evaporator outlet total dissolved solids
notes: AT-LINE, deliberately: an outlet-solids reading is a concentration measurement and is claimed in line nowhere in this register (Q-042 is the reason the distinction is tracked). The evaporator ceiling this would be compared against is itself open (Q-018, P-CONC-EVAP).

purpose: Drying gas inlet temperature
notes: Enforces P-DRY-T-IN. Sets the heater duty, which is the plant utility load (UT-DRYGAS, EQ-ENERGY). The value is an assumption (Q-046).

purpose: Drying gas OUTLET temperature
notes: The instrument that enforces the looser of the two thermal limits on the product: outlet temperature caps the particle's thermal exposure and must sit below the duplex melting temperature (P-DRY-T-OUT, P-DS-TM, Q-030, R-003). The binding limit is the moisture-shifted glass transition, measured by QI-0508.

purpose: Ambient gas temperature upstream of the heater
notes: Monitoring only. P-DRY-T-AMBIENT is the datum the heater duty is measured from, so the utility load moves with it.

purpose: Drying gas mass flow
notes: The drying-gas mass is DERIVED from the process duty in the balance rather than assumed, so this reading is the check on that derivation, not an input to it.

purpose: Atomiser feed flow
notes: Monitoring only at this stage; the atomiser operating range that would bound it is pending atomiser selection (Q-019).

purpose: Exhaust gas humidity
notes: Monitoring only; a drying-endpoint proxy. It is not a substitute for the product moisture measurement below, which is the one the glass transition depends on.

purpose: Product residual moisture (Karl Fischer / loss on drying)
notes: Enforces P-DS-RESID-MOISTURE, and it is half of the binding thermal limit: the 38-53 C glass transition band was measured AT 3.8-4.6% residual moisture, so quoting one without the other detaches the number from its condition (EQ-TG, SRC-KEIL-2021, Q-039). Residual moisture is an OUTCOME of the dryer conditions, not an input, which is why it is measured rather than set.

purpose: Glass transition of the dried powder at its achieved moisture, by DSC
notes: The instrument that enforces the BINDING thermal limit on drying and storage - tighter than the melting temperature (P-DS-TG, EQ-TG). Off-line by nature. The band that exists is for spray-dried trehalose siRNA polyplex formulations, their matrix and their moisture, not ours (Q-039, Q-021).

purpose: Differential pressure across the product-collection filter
notes: Monitoring only. A dried organic powder brings dust-explosion controls into scope (R-016), so collection-filter condition is a safety reading as well as a yield one.

purpose: Full-length and duplex purity of the powder
notes: Monitoring only here, because the analytical dimension the specification will be written in is not chosen (Q-044) - and purity multiplies only within one dimension, so the dimension decides which purity the block-ligation floor must clear (EQ-PURITY, R-003).

purpose: Bioburden on the drug-substance powder
notes: Monitoring only.

purpose: Endotoxin on the drug-substance powder
notes: Monitoring only. What arrives here depends on the protein and endotoxin load entering purification, which depends on the enzyme form (R-017, Q-050).

purpose: CIP return conductivity; cleaning endpoint
notes: Monitoring only. The evaporator and the spray dryer are the hard-to-clean items (R-008).

purpose: CIP supply temperature
notes: Monitoring only.

purpose: CIP loop flow; minimum velocity for surface coverage
notes: Monitoring only; the minimum pump flow that would bound it is a gap (Q-049).

purpose: Residual product in the final CIP rinse
notes: Monitoring only, and it has no acceptance limit: a cleaning-validation limit needs a health-based exposure limit, and P-HBEL-DS is blank because the toxicology data does not exist publicly (Q-047, R-015).
